evidence: This is stated as a result from the anatomical analysis.

claim: Multiglomerular olfactory neurons, and presumptive thermosensory, hygrosensory, and mechanosensory neurons were all concentrated in a ventromedial domain of the LH.
source: Multiglomerular olfactory neurons, and presumptive thermosensory, hygrosensory, and mechanosensory neurons were all concentrated in a ventromedial domain of the LH (Figure 2B), emphasizing that the LH is a multimodal structure.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis.

claim: We identified a total of 261 LHN cell types divided into 34 local cell types (LHLNs) and 227 LHON cell types.
source: We identified a total of 261 LHN cell types divided into 34 local cell types (LHLNs) with arbors restricted to the LH and 227 LHON cell types with axons beyond the LH.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the anatomical classification.

claim: The superior protocerebral neuropils (SLP, SMP and SIP) are the most extensively innervated target areas of LHONs.
source: The superior protocerebral neuropils (SLP, SMP and SIP) are the most extensively innervated; they are the location of 'convergence zones' where direct olfactory output from the LH may be integrated with learned olfactory information from the mushroom body (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis with a citation.

claim: The ventrolateral protocerebrum (AVLP, PVLP) is the next major target of LHONs.
source: The ventrolateral protocerebrum (AVLP, PVLP) is the next major target; this area also receives extensive input from visual projection neurons originating in the optic lobes (e.g. Panser et al., 2016) and is innervated by dendrites of descending neurons, including at least two now known to be downstream of LHONs (Huoviala et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis with citations.

claim: Few LHN cell types project to the contralateral hemisphere.
source: We noticed that few cell types project to the contralateral hemisphere, perhaps because most olfactory projection neurons in the adult fly already receive information from both antennae.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis with speculation.

claim: We annotated LH input neurons from FlyCircuit and divided them into 41 different groups.
source: We annotated LH input neurons from FlyCircuit and divided them into 41 different groups based on the axon tract they use to reach the LH and their pattern of dendritic arborization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B), which we used as a proxy for the modality of the sensory information they encode.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the anatomical classification.

claim: We extended the naming system of Tanaka et al. (2012a) to include 26 types not previously identified.
source: We extended the naming system of Tanaka et al. (2012a) to include 26 types not previously identified (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the nomenclature extension with a citation.

claim: Excitatory uniglomerular and inhibitory GABAergic PNs project widely but spare a ventromedial stripe of the LH.
source: Excitatory uniglomerular and inhibitory GABAergic PNs project widely but spare a ventromedial stripe of the LH, which is the focus of multiglomerular olfactory neurons and other sensory inputs
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis.

claim: Excitatory multiglomerular projection neurons are heavily concentrated in the ventromedial LH.
source: In contrast, excitatory multiglomerular projection neurons are heavily concentrated in the ventromedial LH, where their arbors intermingle with PNs from thermosensory and hygrosensory glomeruli (Frank et al., 2015; Frank et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the anatomical analysis with citations.

claim: The ventral LH receives multimodal input and likely to be involved in multimodal integration while the remainder is predominantly olfactory.
source: In conclusion, the ventral LH receives multimodal input and likely to be involved in multimodal integration while the remainder is predominantly olfactory.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the anatomical analysis.
